_readme: Proof for the numbers and key facts on the slides. Every quote was copied word for word from the page on the date in 'checked' (tools/check-data.mjs keeps 'short' a part of 'quote'); text in [brackets] marks a table or list rebuilt in one line. A tile shows its proof with data-proof="<proof id>" inside <pdac-stat-proof>; a slide lists more with data-proofs; the E key shows every proof on the current slide with a QR code to the page. Module 2's extra sources are the pages its learner guide links to.

proofs.quote: The Cyber Kill Chain is divided into seven stages: reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control (C2), and actions on objectives.
SPF (Sender Policy Framework) is a list of the servers and IP addresses that are allowed to send email on behalf of your domain.
DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) is a cryptographic signature applied to every email you send, which proves the email came from your domain and was not modified in transit.

DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) is a policy that tells receiving mail servers what to do when an email fails SPF or DKIM, and sends you reports about those failures.

Scammers successfully stole HK$200 million (approximately $25.5 million) from a multinational company in Hong Kong by employing a deepfake video call to deceive an employee into transferring the funds.
The employee executed the money transfers during the meeting and transferred around HK$200 million to five bank accounts, with 15 transactions.
